body.statement: Fix \(0<a<\lambda\).  On the \(2\times2\) support, let every response-study observation have a cell label with probability \(1/4\) and, conditional on that label, a Bernoulli response with mean \(\mu_{n,cx}=\lambda/n\).  Let the margins be observed without error, estimate every response mean by an interior \(a/n\)-ridged cell proportion, and use its empirical-influence multiplier with zero margin coordinates.  For every deterministic numerical-delta schedule \(t\), the event that all \(n\) responses are zero has probability tending to \(e^{-\lambda}\); on that event \(L(\beta_n)=U(\beta_n)=\lambda/n\), \(F(\widehat\beta_n)=(a/n,a/n)\), \(q_{1-\alpha,n}^\star=0\), and \([L(\beta_n),U(\beta_n)]\not\subseteq\mathrm{CI}_n(t)\).  Along this array, both the primitive and conditional multiplier bounded-Lipschitz Gaussian discrepancies tend to zero.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(W_i\in\mathcal C\times\mathcal X\) be independent uniform cell labels and let \(Y_i\mid W_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\lambda/n)\), independently for \(i=1,\ldots,n\).  Write \(\overline Y_{n,cx}\) for the response proportion in cell \((c,x)\), setting it to zero for an empty cell, and define
\[
\widehat\mu_{n,cx}
=\left(1-\frac{2a}{n}\right)\overline Y_{n,cx}+\frac{a}{n}.
\tag{19}
\]
For large \(n\), (19) lies strictly between zero and one.  Moreover,
\[
\sqrt n\,|\widehat\mu_{n,cx}-\overline Y_{n,cx}|
\leq\frac{3a}{\sqrt n},
\tag{20}
\]
so the ridge does not alter a root-\(n\) primitive approximation.

Let \(A_n=\{Y_1=\cdots=Y_n=0\}\).  Since every observation has response probability \(\lambda/n\),
\[
\Pr(A_n)=\left(1-\frac{\lambda}{n}\right)^n\longrightarrow e^{-\lambda}.
\tag{21}
\]
On \(A_n\), all estimated costs equal \(a/n\).  Every feasible coupling has mass one, so
\[
L(\beta_n)=U(\beta_n)=\frac{\lambda}{n},
\qquad
F(\widehat\beta_n)=\left(\frac{a}{n},\frac{a}{n}\right).
\tag{22}
\]

Construct \(G_n^\star\) by multiplying the centered empirical cell influence terms for (19) by independent mean-zero, variance-one multipliers, and give it zero margin coordinates.  On \(A_n\), every centered response influence term is zero; hence \(G_n^\star=0\) conditionally.  The ridged estimate and its positive margins are interior, so \(\Pi_{\mathcal B}\) is the identity there.  For every \(t_n>0\),
\[
\widehat F'_n(G_n^\star)=\widehat F'_n(0)=0,
\qquad
q_{1-\alpha,n}^\star=0
\quad\text{on }A_n.
\tag{23}
\]
Thus \(\mathrm{CI}_n(t)=[a/n,a/n]\) on \(A_n\), which misses the true singleton in (22) because \(a\neq\lambda\).

It remains to check that the weak approximations do not exclude this array.  If \(N_{n,cx}\) is a cell count, then on \(N_{n,cx}\geq n/8\),
\[
\operatorname{Var}(\overline Y_{n,cx}\mid N_{n,cx})
\leq\frac{8\lambda}{n^2},
\]
and \(\Pr(N_{n,cx}<n/8)\) is exponentially small.  Hence
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat\mu_n-\mu_n)\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{in }L^1.
\tag{24}
\]
The centered Gaussian having the row primitive covariance also converges to zero in \(L^1\), since that covariance is \(O(n^{-1})\).  The bounded-Lipschitz distance between the two laws is therefore \(o(1)\), by the triangle inequality through the point mass at zero.  Conditionally, the multiplier second moment is \(O_P(K_n/n)\), where \(K_n=\sum_iY_i=O_P(1)\).  Its conditional bounded-Lipschitz distance from the same Gaussian law is consequently \(o_P(1)\), again through zero.  This proves both asserted approximation conclusions while (21) remains bounded away from zero.
